description: This dashboard provides a Detailed DrillDown view of the HDFS NameNode & DataNode status, performance, and resource usage. Metrics are scraped by Prometheus via the jmx-exporter for HDFS NameNode & DataNode deployments.

panels.description:
It reflects the sum of the storage capacity across all DataNodes in the cluster.
 It does not account for disk space reserved for system use or non-HDFS storage. If a new DataNode is added with additional storage, this metric will increase accordingly. If a DataNode fails or is removed, this metric will decrease.
panels.title: Total raw capacity of NameNodes (TB)

panels.description: This metric represents the total amount of free space (in bytes) available across all DataNodes in the cluster. It indicates how much disk space is still available for storing new data in HDFS.
panels.title: Remaining available space (TB)

panels.description: Represents the amount of disk space (in bytes) used for non-HDFS purposes on all DataNodes. Helps track storage that is occupied by non-HDFS files, such as: OS files and logs, Application data (non-HDFS), and Reserved space for system processes.
panels.title: Space used by non-HDFS processes (TB)

panels.description: It represents the percentage of total storage capacity currently in use across all DataNodes in the Hadoop cluster. Helps monitor the disk usage in HDFS and plan for capacity scaling.
panels.title: Percentage of used capacity

panels.description: This metric represents the total number of blocks that have lost all replicas and are currently missing from the cluster. Helps detect data loss scenarios in HDFS where blocks have no available copies on any DataNodes. If MissingBlocks > 0, it indicates potential data loss. Common causes of missing blocks: DataNode failures or disk corruption, Under-replicated blocks due to cluster imbalance, and Accidental deletion of files before replication occurs.
panels.title: Number of missing blocks

panels.description: This metric represents the total number of HDFS blocks that are corrupted and unreadable. Identifies corrupted data blocks in HDFS, which may lead to data loss or access issues. Corrupt blocks indicate possible data integrity issues.  Causes of corruption: Hardware failures (bad sectors on disks), Network transmission errors, Buggy applications writing corrupted data, and Incomplete replication due to DataNode failures.
panels.title: Corrupt block count

panels.description: Represents the number of HDFS blocks currently awaiting replication to meet the configured replication factor. Indicates how many blocks need additional replication, often due to: DataNode failures, Network issues, Disk corruption, and Cluster imbalance. A high PendingReplicationBlocks count suggests data reliability risks if replication is delayed. Normal behavior includes temporary spikes, but persistent high values indicate replication bottlenecks.
panels.title: Blocks pending replication

panels.description: Represents the number of HDFS blocks that have fewer replicas than the configured replication factor but still have at least one copy available. Identifies blocks that are at risk of data loss if more failures occur before replication completes. A high LowRedundancyBlocks count indicates: DataNode failures have reduced replication, Replication is slow or failing due to network/storage issues., and HDFS replication factor is too low for some blocks.
panels.title: Blocks with insufficient replicas

panels.description: Represents the number of slow RPC (Remote Procedure Call) operations on the NameNode. Tracks slow RPC calls, which can indicate performance issues in NameNode processing. A high RpcSlowCalls count suggests: Overloaded NameNode due to excessive client requests, Network congestion slowing down RPC responses, Long GC (Garbage Collection) pauses affecting response times, and Metadata bottlenecks due to large directory listings or slow disk I/O.
panels.title: Count of slow RPC calls

panels.description: Represents the average time (in milliseconds) taken for NameNode edit log sync operations. Tracks the efficiency of NameNode edit log persistence, which directly impacts HDFS metadata performance. High SyncsAvgTime values indicate: Slow disk I/O on the NameNode, Performance bottlenecks in edits log writes, and Potential NameNode checkpointing issues.
panels.title: Average time for journal syncs (ms)

panels.description: Represents the total number of file information lookup operations (getFileInfo) performed on the NameNode. Measures how frequently clients and services request metadata about files in HDFS. A high GetFileInfoNumOps rate could indicate: Heavy client requests querying file metadata, Inefficient application behavior (e.g., excessive file lookups), and Possible NameNode performance bottlenecks.
panels.title: Number of file info retrieval operations

panels.description: Represents the total number of directory listing operations (getListing) performed on the NameNode. Measures how frequently clients and applications request a list of files/directories within an HDFS directory. A high GetListingNumOps rate could indicate: Heavy directory browsing by clients or applications, Inefficient application behavior, such as frequent recursive ls commands, and Potential NameNode performance bottlenecks, especially in large directories.
panels.title: Number of file listing operations

panels.description: Represents the number of active (live) DataNodes currently communicating with the NameNode. Helps monitor HDFS cluster health by tracking the number of DataNodes available for storage and replication. A high NumLiveDataNodes indicates a healthy and well-scaled cluster. A low NumLiveDataNodes or a sudden drop suggests: DataNode failures, Network connectivity issues, Overloaded NameNode, and HDFS misconfiguration.
panels.title: Number of live DataNodes

panels.description: Represents the number of decommissioned DataNodes that are also dead (i.e., DataNodes that were taken out of service and are now unresponsive). Helps track decommissioned DataNodes that have gone offline, which may affect HDFS replication and data availability. A high NumDecomDeadDataNodes value indicates: DataNodes were decommissioned but not removed properly, Some DataNodes crashed during decommissioning, and Potential storage capacity reductions in HDFS.
panels.title: Number of dead DataNodes

panels.description: Represents the current number of open RPC connections to the NameNode. Helps monitor NameNode load and network activity, indicating how many clients and DataNodes are actively communicating with the NameNode. A high NumOpenConnections value suggests: Heavy client or DataNode activity, Potential NameNode overload due to too many concurrent requests, Inefficient application behavior (e.g., frequent metadata lookups), and Possible network congestion. A low or suddenly dropping NumOpenConnections value may indicate: Client disconnections due to network failures, and NameNode service issues causing connection drops.
panels.title: Active connections to the NameNode

panels.description: Measures the amount of heap memory in use by the JVM process. Helps monitor JVM memory usage, ensuring the NameNode has enough memory to handle metadata operations. High heap usage (>80% of max heap) can indicate: Memory leaks in the NameNode process, Large numbers of files and blocks being managed, and Insufficient heap allocation, leading to frequent Garbage Collection (GC) pauses. Low heap usage is normal but can be checked for proper tuning.
panels.title: JVM Heap memory usage (B)

panels.description: Measures the amount of non-heap memory in use by the JVM process. Helps monitor JVM memory usage, particularly for Metaspace, Code Cache, and other JVM internals. Non-heap memory includes: Metaspace: Stores class metadata, Code Cache: Stores compiled JIT code, and Direct Buffers: Used by I/O operations. High non-heap memory usage can indicate: Excessive class loading, possibly due to application memory leaks, Too many active threads, consuming large amounts of Metaspace, and Inefficient JVM memory tuning, causing high non-heap pressure.
panels.title: JVM Non-heap memory usage (B)

panels.description: Measures the used non-heap memory in megabytes. elps monitor JVM memory usage beyond the heap, including Metaspace, Code Cache, and Direct Buffers. Non-heap memory includes: Metaspace: Stores class metadata, Code Cache: Stores Just-In-Time (JIT) compiled code, and Direct Buffers: Used for high-performance I/O operations. High MemNonHeapUsedM values can indicate: Excessive class loading, which can lead to Metaspace exhaustion, Too many active threads, consuming a large amount of JVM resources, and Memory leaks in non-heap allocations.
panels.title: Non-heap memory used (MB)

panels.description: Measures the total time spent by the Parallel Scavenge (PS Scavenge) garbage collector per second. Helps monitor JVM young generation (Eden space) GC activity, ensuring that the NameNode’s memory management is efficient. PS Scavenge GC handles the Young Generation (Eden + Survivor spaces). High values of GcTimeMillisPS_Scavenge indicate: Frequent minor garbage collections (GC), potentially causing performance degradation, Insufficient heap allocation, leading to excessive memory pressure, and Application inefficiencies causing excessive object creation.
panels.title: GC time for minor collections (ms/s)

panels.description: Measures the total time (in ms) the NameNode was paused due to GC-related activity, including extra sleep time imposed by JVM tuning. Helps identify performance bottlenecks caused by GC pauses. High GcTotalExtraSleepTime values indicate: Frequent or long GC pauses, leading to NameNode responsiveness issues, Excessive Full GC events, causing delays in metadata operations, and Potential heap memory misconfiguration. If this value keeps increasing rapidly, it may suggest: NameNode struggling with memory pressure, and Inefficient garbage collection behavior.
panels.title: Total GC extra sleep time (ms)

panels.description: Measures the cumulative CPU usage of the NameNode JVM process. Helps monitor CPU resource consumption of the NameNode process. High process_cpu_seconds_total values indicate: CPU-intensive metadata operations (e.g., excessive file lookups, block reports), Inefficient GC behavior, leading to CPU spikes, Excessive client requests, causing high NameNode workload. If CPU usage suddenly spikes: Could be due to a heavy workload, inefficient queries, or background NameNode operations like safemode checks or block replication tasks.
panels.title: Total CPU time used by NameNode (s)

panels.description: Measures the current CPU usage of the JVM process running the Hadoop NameNode. Helps track how much CPU the NameNode process is consuming in real-time. High CPU load (near 1.0 or 100%) indicates: Heavy NameNode operations, such as: Frequent metadata lookups, High block reporting activity, and Intensive replication tasks. Garbage Collection (GC) overhead consuming CPU cycles. Inefficient client requests overloading the NameNode. Low CPU load is expected during idle periods but should correlate with expected workload.
panels.title: CPU load of the NameNode process

panels.description: Measures the current number of active daemon threads in the JVM. Helps track JVM background thread activity, including Garbage Collection, RPC handling, and internal Hadoop tasks. Daemon threads are JVM-managed threads that run in the background, performing tasks like: Garbage collection (GC), Handling network I/O operations, and Executing Hadoop's internal tasks (e.g., heartbeats, block reports). A sudden increase in daemon threads may indicate: High NameNode workload (e.g., too many client requests), Thread leaks due to misconfigured services, and Inefficient JVM memory management, leading to excessive GC activity.
panels.title: Number of active daemon threads.

panels.description: Measures the total time spent in backoff by RPC clients when they attempt to communicate with the NameNode but are forced to wait due to the NameNode being under heavy load or throttling requests. Helps track the delays or slowdowns in RPC interactions due to server load or throttling. High values of RpcClientBackOff indicate: RPC requests to the NameNode are being delayed due to high traffic or server overload, The NameNode is likely under high load, which could cause increased latency for clients, and Throttling mechanisms might be kicking in to avoid overwhelming the NameNode. Monitoring this metric helps detect: Performance bottlenecks in NameNode operations, Capacity planning issues if the NameNode is not able to handle the required workload.
panels.title: Number of RPC client backoff requests (ms)

panels.description: Tracks the number of RPC requests that were denied due to authorization failures when clients attempted to interact with the NameNode. Helps monitor authorization issues where clients are not authorized to access certain operations on the NameNode. A high number of RpcAuthorizationFailures may indicate: Permission misconfigurations in HDFS, where users or clients are not granted appropriate access, Authentication issues, such as improper Kerberos configurations or invalid tokens, and Unauthorized client operations, where requests from clients are rejected due to insufficient privileges. Tracking authorization failures is important for: Ensuring that the security model in Hadoop is working properly, and Identifying potential security breaches or misconfigurations.
panels.title: Authorization failures

panels.description: Measures the total number of connections to the NameNode that were dropped, either because the client was unable to establish a connection or the connection was closed unexpectedly. Helps monitor the health of network connections between the NameNode and its clients or DataNodes, indicating potential issues with connection stability. High values of NumDroppedConnections could indicate: Network instability, causing connections to be dropped unexpectedly, Server overload, where the NameNode is unable to handle the incoming connections and drops them due to resource constraints, Client timeouts or failed connection attempts due to misconfiguration, and Firewall or security settings blocking or interrupting connections. This metric is important for: Ensuring reliable communication between NameNode and other components of the Hadoop ecosystem (like DataNodes, clients, etc.), and Identifying and troubleshooting network issues or resource bottlenecks.
panels.title: Dropped client connections

panels.description: Tracks how many pending block reconstruction operations have timed out due to delays, often because of unavailable or slow DataNodes, or a lack of sufficient replicas to complete the reconstruction. Helps monitor block reconstruction tasks that are delayed or failing due to timeouts, indicating potential issues with the HDFS infrastructure, such as failed DataNodes, network issues, or insufficient replication. High values of NumTimedOutPendingReconstructions indicate: Block reconstruction is failing due to a lack of available DataNodes or sufficient replicas to reconstruct lost or under-replicated blocks, Slow or unresponsive DataNodes that delay block recovery processes, and Network issues causing timeouts in communication between the NameNode and DataNodes. This metric is crucial for: Ensuring the health of the HDFS block replication process, Identifying infrastructure issues such as DataNode failures or network latency that prevent timely reconstruction, and Preventing data loss by ensuring HDFS can repair under-replicated blocks efficiently.
panels.title: Timed-out block reconstructions

title: HDFS NameNode / DataNode Drilldown
